senses.gloss: If two goals, plans, meetings, etc. conflict, they both cannot be achieved, work or be true.
examples: The goal of hiring more workers conflicts with the plan to cut costs.
Sorry, the meeting conflicts with my prior plans.

senses.gloss: Consultation is the process of getting advice or opinions from other people.
examples: The city went through the planning process with very little public consultation.
The group announced the price per kilo of grapes after consultation with the growers.

senses.gloss: A challenge is something difficult that you want or have to do.
examples: Many churches overseas are struggling to meet the AIDS challenge.
After 25 years in the same job, this move will allow me to take on new challenges.

senses.gloss: A challenge is an offer to compete or fight.
examples: The president issued a challenge to his critics to appear in a public debate.

senses.gloss: If you challenge somebody, you give them something very difficult to do.
examples: The job challenges his computer skills.

senses.gloss: If you challenge somebody, you offer to compete or fight.
examples: He challenged me to a game of chess.

senses.gloss: If you cite people or facts, you write or talk about them to support your point or show where you got your information.
examples: Larkin (1979) cites cases of families who have moved out of regular homes into mobile homes or campers.
Two thirds of the people cited unemployment as the `main issue'.

senses.gloss: If someone is cited by the police, they are ordered to appear before the court.
A case is a container to hold something.
examples: He opened the case and pulled out his violin.

senses.gloss: A case is a matter for police or in court.
examples: The judge did not accept his case.

senses.gloss: If a police officer cases a house, he or she watches it until something happens.
examples: We were casing a house all night in Brooklyn.

senses.gloss: A class is a time for learning.
examples: The history class is interesting.
Class today will be about whole numbers.

senses.gloss: A class is a group of students.
examples: They are my best class because they are always here on time.
Class sizes are usually larger in high school.

senses.gloss: If something is classed as a member of a group, it belongs to that group because of some characteristics shared by the group's members.
examples: Although it looks like a motorcycle, it is officially classed as a car.

senses.gloss: A class act is high quality .
examples: Most high school coaches are class individuals, and they should get our thanks.

senses.gloss: A compliment is a few words of praise: saying that someone or something is good in some way.
examples: William gave me a compliment and that made me feel good. He told me my hair was nice.

senses.gloss: Compliment means to praise someone.
examples: She complimented him on his clothes because they looked good.

senses.gloss: A conjunction is a word used to join words, phrases, clauses, or sentences.
examples: The word or is a conjunction because it can join two words: Tell me if you see a red or blue car.
The word that can be used as a conjunction: I think that you are right.

senses.gloss: Three common conjunctions
A conviction is when a court finds a person guilty of doing a crime.
examples: There was a conviction in his case, so he went to jail.

senses.gloss: A conviction is a strong belief that you think is true.
examples: Because of their strong conviction, I begin to feel that they may be right.

senses.gloss: If you have control over someone or something, you can make it do what you want.
examples: He should try to take control and tell the other handlers what to do.
Driving in the rain, he had lost control on the wet surface and spun off the road.

senses.gloss: A control is a button, switch, dial, etc. that lets you make a machine do what you want.
examples: If you turn off your TV with the remote control, it continues to use a quarter of normal power.
She touched the volume control and the sound dropped.

senses.gloss: If you control something, you make it do what you want.
examples: Too many people are overweight because they can't control their eating behaviour.
The company is controlled by a New York businessman.

senses.gloss: If you control something, you do not let its numbers or size grow too much.
examples: The new plan should control inflation.

senses.gloss: To move towards a place or into a place; to move to the place where the person who is talking is.
examples: Come to my house and I will give you something to eat.
Come here to me.

senses.gloss: The past participle of come.
When something happens or arrives.
examples: We'll talk again come January.

senses.gloss: Semen.
examples: (also spelled cum)

senses.gloss: A clear idea is an idea that is easy to understand.
examples: OK, so you need the key. I see. That's clear now.
Now it's clear as a bell to me why you want to stay here.

senses.gloss: If it is clear that something is a certain way, there can be no mistake about it.
examples: The women made it clear that they were doing this only because they wanted to.
It soon became perfectly clear that he was not going to get better.

senses.gloss: If you clear something, you move or remove things that you don't want there.
examples: You clear the table and I'll get coffee ready.
We'll have to clear out the garage to make room for the new car.

senses.gloss: If something clears, it becomes clear.
examples: After the fire, it took some time for the air to clear.
Above her, the black sky cleared, until she could see the thousands of stars all across it.

senses.gloss: Out of, away from, especially too far away to be noticed or caught.
examples: After a short walk, we were clear of the town.
The fish was so heavy that he couldn't get it clear of the water.

senses.gloss: Completely, without limit.
examples: You could see clear across the water, all the way to the church 60 km away on the other side.

senses.gloss: Something that is covering another thing is on top of (or over) the other thing in a way that stops people from seeing it.
examples: I cover myself in two blankets at night to stay warm.
Remember to cover the pot with a lid while you're cooking something.

senses.gloss: A cover is something that usually covers something else.
examples: The cover of the book has a picture on it under the name of the book.

senses.gloss: When something cracks it breaks along a line, maybe not a straight line. It might break into two pieces, or it might break but the two pieces are still attached.
examples: She cracked an egg and put the inside of the egg into a bowl.

senses.gloss: A crack is the line where something is breaking.
examples: There is a crack from the edge of this plate to the middle. It will break soon.

senses.gloss: A loud sound like the sound of something breaking.
examples: It was raining, and she saw a flash of lightning and heard the crack of thunder.

senses.gloss: If someone or something is capable of something, they can do it.
examples: This system is capable of providing food for about 400 people.
I'm quite capable of looking after myself and I don't need you to tell me how.

senses.gloss: If someone is capable, they can do a particular thing well.
examples: I'm confident I can leave everything in your capable hands.
I may be young but I can assure you I'm quite capable.

senses.gloss: A person moves a comb through their hair many times to make their hair look nice.
examples: Joe always had a comb in his pocket.

senses.gloss: To move a comb through hair.
examples: I washed and combed my hair.

senses.gloss: To look carefully for something.
examples: The police combed the forest for the person but didn't find him.

senses.gloss: A cushion is a pillow; a soft item that people can sit on or put their head on when they lie down.
examples: Here's a bed with sheets, a cushion and a blanket.
Here's a soft chair with two cushions to make it even softer.

senses.gloss: To stop one item from making hard contact with another item.
examples: Mats were laid down to cushion the gymnast's fall.

senses.gloss: When someone makes a comparison between two things, the person thinks about how the two things are the same and how they are different, which one is bigger etc.
examples: I need to make some comparisons between different houses before I make a decision about which house to buy.
A careful comparison will show that this cup has a little more water than the other cup.

senses.gloss: A curve is a line that is not straight. It is like part of a circle. It starts in one direction and turns.
examples: The edge of the flower petal is a beautiful curve.

senses.gloss: To move in a curve.
examples: The car curved around the corner.
This piece of wood is not good. It is curved.

senses.gloss: Copper is a metal that is a red-brown colour. Sometimes coins of small value are made from copper. The symbol for copper is Cu with an atomic number of 29.
examples: Water comes into our house through copper pipes.

senses.gloss: A copper is a penny, a coin of small value made of copper.
examples: Could you give me a copper? I have almost enough money to buy that thing.

senses.gloss: Made of copper.
examples: The copper statue has turned green.

senses.gloss: Having the reddish-brown colour/color of copper
examples: The copper couch will look really nice with that wallpaper.

senses.gloss: In a cooperative effort, project, etc., a number of people work together to do something.
examples: Development of the machine became a cooperative effort between university and industry in the UK.

senses.gloss: If someone is cooperative, they listen and try to help or work with you.
examples: He was very hard to work with, but recently has become much more cooperative.

senses.gloss: A cooperative is a type of business that is owned by the people working there or by its customers.
examples: Mountain Equipment Co-op (MEC), a retail co-operative, is Canada's largest supplier of outdoor equipment and has more than two million members.

senses.gloss: A company is an organization for doing work for money.
examples: He works for a big company.
I own this company, so it's a problem for me if people don't buy what we make.

senses.gloss: Company is people who are visiting other people; people who are in other peoples' house so that they can talk to the other people, or people who are walking with other people or being somewhere with other people.
examples: I can't talk to you on the phone right now, because I have company. (people in the house.)

senses.gloss: Someone who is cruel is mean. They hurt other people and don't care, or they like hurting other people.
examples: The cruel guard pushed the prisoners so hard that some of them fell down.

senses.gloss: An action is cruel if only cruel people would do it.
examples: It's cruel to make children work 10 hours a day.

senses.gloss: An outer piece of clothing that covers the upper part of the body and the arms.
examples: The woman wore a fur coat.
It's cold today, so you need to wear a coat when you go outside.

senses.gloss: A covering of material, such as paint.
examples: He applied a thin coat of paint to the wood.

senses.gloss: To cover with a coat (2) of some material
examples: A person can buy coated frying pans, which are much easier to wash up than normal ones.

senses.gloss: To cover as a coat (2).
examples: Thick paint coated the wall.

senses.gloss: A condition is a logical clause or phrase that a conditional statement uses. The phrase can either be true or false.
The health status of a medical patient.
examples: The doctor will check my condition.

senses.gloss: To become accustomed to changes in the environment.
examples: I became conditioned to the weather in San Diego.

senses.gloss: To subject to different conditions, especially as an exercise.
examples: They were conditioning their shins in their karate class.

senses.gloss: If you close something, you change it from being open to not open.
examples: She watched TV for a while, and then closed her eyes.
He left the room and softly closed the door behind him.

senses.gloss: If something closes, it goes out of business for a short time or permanently.
examples: The supermarket closes at 5 o'clock on Saturday.
Sadly, we have decided to close the shop.

senses.gloss: When two things are close, they are near each other; the distance or time between them is small.
examples: The bank is close to the store.
I walk to my university because it is very close.

senses.gloss: If two people are close, they have a good relationship, like friends, family or lovers.
examples: She was quite close to her dad before he died.

senses.gloss: If a game or contest is close, you can't easily see which side is better.
examples: The race has been very close up until now.

senses.gloss: The close of something is the end.
examples: I will be surprised if the company is still running by close of business tomorrow.
The book was written around the close of the 14th century.

senses.gloss: When something is crucial, it is very important. It will make a big difference. You cannot succeed without it.
examples: To write a great book, it's crucial to have the person in the book change and develop.
It was a crucial time in the battle when the king dropped his sword.

senses.gloss: Something collapses when all its parts fall down loosely. A building or a bridge collapses when it breaks and all its parts fall down. A person collapses when they are tired and they fall into a chair or onto a bed and are too tired to get up.
examples: He was so tired, he just collapsed onto that chair.
The bridge collapsed, but no one was hurt.

senses.gloss: The act of collapsing.
examples: The collapse of the bridge means we can't go over the river any longer.

senses.gloss: A colleague is a person who works together with another person or who does the same kind of work.
examples: I like to talk about the science with my colleagues from the other university.

senses.gloss: A small coin of little value, also called a penny; 100 cents make a dollar.
examples: This gum only costs five cents.

senses.gloss: When there is a controversy about something, people don't agree about it and there is a lot of talking about it.
examples: There's a controversy about whether cars should be allowed to drive in this part of the city.
Newspapers love to write about controversies.

senses.gloss: Clumsiness is a lack of coordination; it is the condition of being clumsy.
Someone compiles some things or ideas when they bring them together into one place.
examples: I need to compile a list of reasons not to go ahead with the project.
She compiled a good set of books to read about the history of that place.

senses.gloss: If you can conceive of a certain situation, you can imagine it.
examples: I just can't conceive of life without you.
Can you conceive what life would have been like in that time?

senses.gloss: Someone conceives of an idea when they think of the idea for the first time, and it's their idea: they thought of it themselves, no one told them.
examples: The planners first conceived of the idea of making a large, curved building here in 1998.
I can't conceive of any way of getting there before 5:00.

senses.gloss: A hundredth of a meter; 100 centimeters is one meter.
examples: This pencil is 18 centimeters long.

senses.gloss: A church where a bishop is based.
examples: The new bishop took control of his cathedral.

senses.gloss: A channel is a path that carries or directs flow or movement, especially of TV & radio signals and water.
examples: He only watches two television news channels.

senses.gloss: The bottom and sides ("banks") of a river or other place where water moves.
If you channel something, you direct its flow.
examples: We will channel the cars to the left.

senses.gloss: To take on the personality of another person.
examples: When it is my turn to sing Karaoke, I am going to channel Ray Charles.

senses.gloss: To make someone believe, or feel sure about something.
examples: We have to convince her that the world is a sphere.

senses.gloss: If you convert something, you change it so that it has a different function or form.
examples: They wanted to convert the room into a study.
The factory was powered originally by water, then converted to steam in 1811.

senses.gloss: A convert is a person who changed their beliefs or religion.
examples: Mr Kinnock is a relatively recent convert to Buddhism.
And we must not discount those who became converts to the new religion.

senses.gloss: If x comprises y, y is part of x.
examples: The United States comprises Hawaii and Alaska.

senses.gloss: If x comprises y, y is all the things that, together, make x.
examples: The United States comprises 50 states.

senses.gloss: Confidence is the state of trusting something, and being sure that something is going to happen.
examples: I know you're trying to gain confidence in what you're doing.

senses.gloss: If something is comprehensive, it includes everything that is related.
examples: The book includes the most comprehensive list of existing government programs.
This chapter is not intended to provide a detailed and comprehensive documentation of the aids available in the UK.

senses.gloss: If an act or idea is contrary to something, it is against it.
examples: The president's actions are contrary to the constitution and therefore illegal.

senses.gloss: You use contrary to x when x is different from the truth.
examples: Contrary to popular belief, the oil companies cannot control the price of crude.
What she told me was contrary to everything I had ever heard.

senses.gloss: A contrary view, sentence, etc. is opposite to other ones.
examples: The contrary view is that these kind of projects are a waste of money.
The only thoughts he had were contrary ones.

senses.gloss: A contrary person tries to be different from other people or does not often agree with others.
Someone who shows cowardice is being afraid, not having courage, not doing something they should do because they are afraid.
examples: He showed cowardice when he ran away and left his friend to fight the other children.

senses.gloss: Two things coincide with each other if they're both in the same place or at the same time.
examples: The time of your party coincides with my niece's wedding, so I can't come.
The end of one side of a triangle coincides with the end of another side, making a corner.

senses.gloss: If something commences, it begins.
examples: The school year commenced on Sept. 4.

senses.gloss: Clarity is the quality of being clear.
examples: She dreamed, with great clarity, that she had seen her own death.
Lack of clarity on the part of the teacher will cause confusion among the students.

senses.gloss: Conformity is the state of being or becoming similar to other members of a group.
examples: In high school, students who do not show a high degree of conformity are often not accepted by other students.
Often the teaching of writing is really the teaching of social conformity: students must write like everyone else.

senses.gloss: Conformity is the state of following rules or expectations.
examples: The army is there to ensure conformity with the UN resolutions.

senses.gloss: If something is contemporary it is related to this time (now). Technically, this is an incorrect usage; better is to use "modern", "now" or "present-day".
examples: The artist has a great knowledge of the sources of historical and contemporary art.

senses.gloss: If x is contemporary with y, they happened at about the same time.
examples: They are sources that are contemporary or near contemporary with the period being studied.

senses.gloss: Somebody's contemporary is a person who lived at or near the same time.
examples: This is what made Marx so different from his socialist contemporaries.

senses.gloss: A commodity is something that is bought or sold.
examples: The price of corn and other farming commodities has dropped by 10%.
There have been big changes in commodity prices and exchange rates over the past decade.

senses.gloss: A commodity is a valuable quality or thing.
examples: Hope may become a very rare commodity.

senses.gloss: If something is challenging, it is not easy but it can be done.
examples: For a longer, wilder and more challenging route, you can explore the beautiful mountains around Goatfell.
All actors will agree that Hamlet is a very challenging role.

senses.gloss: The present participle of challenge.
A chart is information that is organised in rows and columns or as a picture.
examples: In India as a whole the figure is about 40% (see chart).
This week's bar chart shows the correct figures.

senses.gloss: (often plural) A chart is a list of most popular songs, movies, etc. that is published regularly.
examples: This week, the newest Star Wars movie is topping the charts.

senses.gloss: If you chart something, you record it in a chart.
If something charts, it is on a list of most popular things.
A currency is the money from a particular country.
examples: A person going abroad can obtain foreign currency notes and travellers' cheques from his own bank.
The US dollar ended lower against most other currencies in London.

senses.gloss: If something has currency, it is generally accepted.
examples: After the war, these new ideas began to gain currency.

senses.gloss: If you cease something, you stop doing it.
examples: Around the time of the First World War, Clark brothers ceased operations, and the mill finally fell silent.
Beyond the window, the rain ceased, giving way to sunshine.

senses.gloss: If two things are concurrent, they happen at the same time.
examples: The software can handle up to 500 concurrent users.
He was given six concurrent three-month jail sentences for the attacks.

senses.gloss: If two things are concurrent, they agree in meaning.
examples: The police got concurrent stories from five witnesses.

senses.gloss: Conversely is used to say that one idea is the opposite of the other idea.
examples: The over-confident driver may drive too fast. Conversely the under-confident person may also cause problems by driving too slowly.

senses.gloss: If you confine someone or something to a particular topic or activity, you do not let them do other topics or activities.
examples: Humphrey did not confine his activities just to the factory.
Her relatively short life was largely confined to Copenhagen.

senses.gloss: If you confine somebody or something, you put them in a place that they cannot leave.
examples: For the first twenty years he was confined in prison-like conditions.
The disease was confined to a small area within the Camperdown district.

senses.gloss: Coherence is the property of being connected, especially of ideas.
examples: Even if the story lacks logical coherence, it is still a fun film to watch.
Teachers need to help the learner to achieve a genuine sense of coherence across the subjects.

senses.gloss: A person who makes crossword puzzles.
A person who enjoys doing crossword puzzles.
examples: Susan is a cruciverbalist; she does the newspaper crossword puzzle every day.

senses.gloss: A contributor is a person who donates money to a charity or a cause.
examples: I am a contributor to Red Cross.

senses.gloss: A contributor is a person who supports or participates in a cause, activity or institution.
examples: He was a regular contributor to anti-war protests.

senses.gloss: The cost of something is the price that a person pays for it.
examples: What is the cost of the car?

senses.gloss: When you say that a thing costs, you say that one must pay in order to buy it.
examples: That diamond ring costs a great deal of money.

senses.gloss: One may say that an action costs a certain bad result.
examples: It cost me my job when I broke the machine.
To commit a crime will cost you.

senses.gloss: A catch is something that is caught, like the fish a fishermen catches.
examples: My dad brought home a good catch of trout today.

senses.gloss: A catch is old time word for a song.
examples: We sang a catch by Purcell.

senses.gloss: When you catch something, you stop and hold it.
examples: Can you catch a fish in your hands with no fish net?

senses.gloss: The past tense and past participle of catch.
A court is where people are tried for crimes.
examples: The bad guy goes to court to stand before the judge.

senses.gloss: A court is an open space where certain games are played.
examples: Tennis is played on a court.

senses.gloss: When one person courts another, that person does things to get the other to like him or her.
examples: The boy sent flowers to court the girl.

senses.gloss: A thing is central when it is in the middle.
examples: The house is central to all of the stores.
The bazaar is central to the city .

senses.gloss: When you choose a thing, you decide you want it and not something else.
examples: The manager and coaches will choose the starting line-up.
Rafferty always chooses those with the best skills.

senses.gloss: If you call someone, you contact them using a telephone.
examples: Can you call me tonight at about 8:00?
We called 911 and the police came in five minutes.

senses.gloss: If you call to someone, you use your voice to make them notice you.
examples: I can't see you. Call out to me so I can find you.
